info.name: STX API Key APIs
info.description:
Every GraphQL operation available to API-key authentication.

SETUP -- set these collection variables:
  server_url            https://staging.on.sportsxapp.com
  STX-ACCESS-KEY        your Key ID from Account > API Keys
  STX-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP  current Unix time in milliseconds
  STX-ACCESS-SIGNATURE  base64 Ed25519 signature of <timestamp>POST/api/graphql

The timestamp and signature expire after 30 seconds, so regenerate them before each send. Postman's sandbox has no Ed25519 implementation, so generate them outside Postman -- see the API Key Authentication guide for a helper script.

Folder 1 needs no authentication at all -- send those requests with only the Content-Type header. Folders 2 and 3 require the three signed headers; folder 3 additionally requires a read_write key.

ENDPOINTS
  GraphQL    {{server_url}}{{graphql_path}}   e.g. https://staging.on.sportsxapp.com/api/graphql
  WebSocket  {{ws_url}}{{socket_path}}?vsn=2.0.0

WEBSOCKET AUTH
Postman cannot store WebSocket requests in a shared collection, so create one with New > WebSocket, point it at the URL above, and add three headers:
  X-STX-ACCESS-KEY, X-STX-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP, X-STX-ACCESS-SIGNATURE
Note the X- prefix, which the HTTP requests do not use, and that the signed message is <timestamp>GET/socket/websocket -- method GET, and WITHOUT the ?vsn= query string. No token parameter is needed: ?token= is for session logins, not API keys.
Public market data channels need no headers at all.

Not included: loyalty, casino, payments, authentication and 2FA, profile, devices and limits, and the session-only placeOddsOrder / placeRiskOrder. Those either are not callable with an API key or are not part of trading.

Questions: https://discord.gg/yF9eVzPzNZ
